name: Jarrod M. Hicks
intro: I study how our brains turn sounds into meaning, and I also make fun perception content.
description: Jarrod M. Hicks studies how the brain turns sound into meaning. Postdoctoral fellow at the University of Rochester.
about: I'm a postdoctoral fellow working with Sam Norman-Haignere at the University of Rochester, supported by an [NIH F32 fellowship](https://reporter.nih.gov/search/QzmxsH50-USvNdKz_gkXcg/project-details/11459751). Before that I did my PhD at MIT with Josh McDermott studying the perception of sound textures (e.g., running water, chirping birds, wind blowing, etc.) and their role in auditory scene analysis.
I record from the human brain, measure behavior, and build computational models to understand how we make sense of sound.
Outside the lab I enjoy teaching, outreach and making content about perception under the name [psychophyshicks](http://youtube.com/@psychophyshicks).
